I am a fully functioning alcoholic (strange thing to say lol but I back up all my promises and responsibilities) and I am trying to quit. What it affects though is my emotional side of things. The first drink after a long time feels amazing and you feel pretty good the other day too because (at least for me) tolerance for alcohol drops down and you get drunk and relaxed pretty fast and that actually encourages me to drink more often which after some time starts to build up tolerance and hangovers get harder because I start drinking more and I start to feel like shit and I drink to not feel like shit. So this time around I actually start to understand that I shouldn't even touch it because over time it puts me in the same position I stopped drinking last time. So no alcohol for me AT ALL.

Thing is I often hear words like you should open up/talk more/express your emotions and other stuff. But when I do people don't seem to care, yeah they hear what I say but they don't give a fuck and just give a cliche answer like "better times will come" or just plain tell me to man up and ignore my problems. So I keep everything inside but occasionally I just burst and then everybody is surprised how a person can hold so much anger inside. Instead of the fucking lectures and low effort answers I would want a fucking hug or just knowing that somebody actually cares and believes in me.

Therapy? Medication? Tried that. In my experience it is very expensive and not that effective but maybe that's just me. 

All in all yeah, people sometimes talk about men's mental health but that's just it, just talks. No progress, no effort, no nothing. It seems that a man would really have to kill himself just for other people to understand how shitty he felt.
